article.title: Government notifies a 12% safeguard duty on flat steel imports for 200 days
article.text: The finance ministry notified a twelve per cent provisional safeguard duty on imports of hot-rolled and cold-rolled flat steel products for two hundred days, acting on the directorate general of trade remedies' preliminary finding of serious injury from a surge in low-priced shipments. Landed import parity for flat products rises immediately by roughly the duty, which restores pricing headroom for domestic mills that had been discounting to hold share. Tata Steel and JSW Steel together account for the majority of domestic flat-product capacity. Downstream converters that buy hot-rolled coil, including auto component makers and pipe manufacturers, face a higher input cost with contracts that reprice only at quarter end.
article.note: Protection is a transfer, not a creation: the mill's gain is the converter's cost. The converter side is real but reaches the graph with nothing company-specific behind it.

shocks.label: Import tariff increase
shocks.mechanism: A safeguard duty lifts landed import parity, transferring pricing power from importers and downstream converters to domestic producers of the protected product

companies.name: Tata Steel
companies.mechanism: Domestic flat-product realisation is set at import parity, so a twelve per cent duty restores the discount the mill had been giving up to hold share against low-priced imports
companies.rationale: Large Indian flat-product capacity priced directly against the imports now dutiable

companies.name: Bharat Forge
companies.mechanism: Steel is the principal raw material for forged components and a higher domestic price raises input cost until quarter-end contract repricing catches up
companies.rationale: Downstream converter of the protected product

companies.name: JSW Steel
companies.mechanism: The largest domestic flat-product capacity competes head-on with the dutiable import stream, so the duty converts directly into realisation per tonne on unchanged volumes
companies.rationale: Largest exposure to the exact product category the duty covers

ground_truth.rationale: The mill named by the article publishes at distance 1. The converter's loss is economically real and the system still must not publish it: nothing company-specific supports it -- no exposure record, no relationship artifact, not even a mention -- so it is model inference, which caps materiality at LOW and authorises nothing. Precision-first means eating a true negative rather than guessing a true positive.
